title: Develop and manage IT security, privacy, and data protection
goal: The venture knows what personal and confidential data each system holds, under which rules, who may reach it and for how long it is kept, and each security control over that data has been checked on a date.

steps.do: For each system, write what personal or confidential data it holds, whose it is, which rule covers it (from the obligations record and the provider's own data terms) and what the venture promised about it in writing, citing each source and date and sending anything you cannot source to the founder and counsel.

Write who decides what about this data here: that the founder alone accepts a provider's data terms, widens access to customer data or approves a deletion, and that you may only narrow access, taking the classes from the venture's decision rights.

Write the venture's data rules on one page: what is collected and why, who and which agent role may read each class of it, how long each class is kept, when it is deleted, and how a person's request about their own data is answered.

Check and record, per system, whether its data is encrypted at rest and in transit by the provider's own account, who can export it, whether any copy sits on a personal device or an unmanaged drive, and whether a secret ever appears in a record or a repository.

Check the venture's own applications and the agent paths into them: that each role authenticates as itself, that no credential is shared between a person and an agent, that dependencies are at a supported version, and that nothing writes a record outside the router's gate.

Check the physical side this venture actually has: which devices hold its records or credentials, whether each has disk encryption and a screen lock, and what happens to a device that is lost or sold.

consider.why: A laptop or phone that holds the venture's credentials is the whole physical perimeter of a small venture, and a server room is not.
consider.when: A device other than the founder's own holds the venture's records or credentials.

steps.do: Read what the providers already report (sign-in alerts, new-device notices, token use from an unexpected place, failed login bursts) and for each, write what it was, what it reached and what you changed, carrying out only the narrowing and telling the founder at once when customer data may have been reached.

consider.why: The providers' own alerts are free and are the only intrusion signal a small venture has; a detection product is not worth buying yet.
consider.when: A provider has sent a security alert, or a system holds customer data.

steps.do: Record each check and each alert as evidence on the decision it bears on, propose the order of fixes to the product lead, and raise for the founder every widening of access to personal data, every set of data terms and every deletion.

done_criteria.check: Does every system say what personal or confidential data it holds, under which sourced rule, who may reach it and how long it is kept, and does every security check carry its date and result?
